templates.title: Relationship Basics
templates.summary: Five Aspects of a relationship — time, housework, money, conflict and affection — each answered from how it feels now to how you wish it to change.

items.prompt: How much time do you spend together in a normal week?
How is the work of the household divided?
How are money and the decisions about it handled?
When there is a disagreement, how is it raised?
How often do you show affection?

templates.title: Staff & Manager
templates.summary: Relationship Type: Business — the glossary's Staff / Manager descriptor, Realm: Office. Five Aspects of a working relationship — priorities, feedback, workload, decisions and development — each answered from how it feels now to how you wish it to change.

items.prompt: How are the week's priorities agreed?
How is feedback on the work given?
How is the workload split between the two of you?
How are the decisions about the work made?
How much do you talk about growth and what comes next?

templates.title: Parent & Child
templates.summary: Relationship Type: Personal — the glossary's Parent / Child descriptor, Realm: Home. Five Aspects of raising a child together — check-ins, house rules, trust, one-to-one time and privacy — each answered from how it feels now to how you wish it to change.

items.prompt: How often do you check in about their day?
How are the house rules agreed?
How much do you trust their judgement?
How much one-to-one time do you spend?
How much privacy do they get?
items.rightValue: As much as they ask for

templates.title: Untitled Relationship
templates.summary: Relationship Type: ________ — left blank, because this template is the user's to name; the glossary it fills lists Business, Personal and a third line. Five unnamed Aspects, each with a prompt and two Values to overwrite before this is copied into a Relationship.

items.prompt: Aspect 1 — what should this ask?
Aspect 2 — what should this ask?
Aspect 3 — what should this ask?
Aspect 4 — what should this ask?
Aspect 5 — what should this ask?

templates.title: Coworker–Colleague
templates.summary: Two coworkers who share work and want the handovers and the credit to feel fair.

items.prompt: How well do work handovers between you actually work?
How much do you each know about what the other is working on?
When a shared result lands, how is credit handled?
When you disagree about how to do something, how does it get resolved?
How reliably do the commitments you make to each other hold?

templates.title: Business Partner A–Business Partner B
templates.summary: Two business partners who want the split of decisions and money out in the open.

items.prompt: How clearly are decision rights split between you?
How much does each of you know about the business's actual money position?
How fairly does the effort each of you puts in compare to what each expected?
When you disagree about the business, what happens?
How clear is what happens if one of you wants out?
How aligned are your appetites for risk right now?

templates.title: Project Manager–Team Member
templates.summary: A project manager and a team member on the same project.

items.prompt: How close is the plan to what can actually be delivered?
How clear is which work comes first?
When something blocks the work, how fast does it get raised and cleared?
How much latitude does each of you have over how the work is done?
How honest is the status each of you reports?

templates.title: Project Teammate A–Project Teammate B
templates.summary: Two teammates on the same project whose work meets in the middle.

items.prompt: How well-defined is the boundary where your work meets?
How much are your own priorities disrupted by each other?
How close is the standard each of you holds to the other's?
When the project lands, how is credit shared?
When one of you drops something, how is it handled?

templates.title: Customer–Vendor Product
templates.summary: A customer and a product vendor checking whether the product delivers what was bought.

items.prompt: How close is what the product does to what the customer expected?
When something goes wrong, how reachable is real help?
How does the price compare to the value each side thinks it delivers?
How much can the customer influence what gets built next?
How likely is each of you to continue the arrangement?

templates.title: Customer–Vendor Services
templates.summary: A customer and a services vendor checking whether the engagement is working on both sides.

items.prompt: How clearly is the scope of the work written down?
How reliably are the committed dates met?
When the customer wants something added, how does that get handled?
How predictable are the updates each side gets?
How well do the payment terms match what each side expected?

templates.title: Investor–SponsorEntrepreneur
templates.summary: An investor and a founder who want the reporting and the decision rights to feel honest.

items.prompt: How predictable and honest is the reporting the investor gets?
How well does the investor's involvement match what the founder wants?
How quickly does bad news travel between you?
How aligned are your time horizons?
How clear is who decides what?
How well do the agreed terms match what both understood at the time?

templates.title: Co-founders
templates.summary: Two people building something together.

items.prompt: How is ownership of the company divided?
How are the big decisions about the product made?
How is the work split between the two of you?
When you disagree about direction, how is it resolved?
How are money drawn and reinvested decided?
How much do you each know about the other's work?
What happens to the company if one of you leaves?

templates.title: HOA Board Member–Owner
templates.summary: An HOA board member and an owner checking whether the property is being run fairly.

items.prompt: How clear is what the fees are spent on?
How clear are the rules that apply to owners?
How much can an owner influence a board decision?
How quickly does the board respond to an owner's issue?
How consistently are rules applied across owners?
How does the state of shared property compare to what owners were told?

templates.title: Parent–Teacher
templates.summary: A parent and a teacher who want the picture of the child to match on both sides.

items.prompt: How clear a picture does the parent have of how the child is doing?
How easy is it for either of you to raise something?
How well does what happens at home match what the classroom needs?
How aligned are your expectations of the child?
When there is a concern, how is it raised?

templates.title: Teacher–Student

items.prompt: How clear is what is expected of the student, week to week?
How useful is the feedback each of you gets?
How safe is it for the student to say they do not understand?
How well does the pace match what the student can actually absorb?
How much is genuine effort noticed?

templates.title: Patient–Caregiver

items.prompt: How much say does the patient have in decisions about their own care?
How well informed does each of you feel about what is happening?
How fairly is the day-to-day load distributed?
How well does the current arrangement respect what the patient wants kept private?
How much real relief does each of you get?
How able are you to bring in help when it is needed?

templates.title: Spouse A–Spouse B

How much say does each of you have over money decisions?
How does the time you actually spend together compare to what each wants?
When you argue, how well do you get back to normal?
How comfortable is each of you with the other's friendships and family time?
How aligned are your pictures of the next few years?
